claims.title: Exact total-variation mass-transport expectation theorem
claims.scope: one finite rational nominal probability vector, one rational state-value vector, and one rational total-variation radius in the unit interval
assumptions: total variation is one half of L1 distance on the finite simplex
the objective is the expectation of a fixed state-value vector
probability may be reallocated to any state in the declared finite support
nonclaims: the theorem concerns a linear expectation and does not solve arbitrary nonlinear risk functionals
a TV ambiguity set is a declared uncertainty model rather than an empirically justified confidence region by itself

claims.title: Exact primal-dual threshold certificate for TV transport
claims.scope: the finite rational TV-ball expectation problem reduced to a bounded fractional-knapsack donor problem
assumptions: maximizing mass may be placed on a maximum-value state and minimizing mass on a minimum-value state
removed mass from each donor is bounded by its nominal probability
the TV budget is an upper bound and may be slack after saturation
nonclaims: the threshold dual is not asserted for nonlinear objectives without a separate reduction
a zero rational gap certifies the declared finite optimization problem rather than a physical implementation claim

claims.title: Piecewise-linear TV expectation profile with saturation and exact range window
claims.scope: one finite rational nominal law and fixed rational value vector as the TV radius varies from zero to one
assumptions: donor states are exhausted in increasing value order for maximization and decreasing value order for minimization
adjacent equal-slope transport intervals may be merged
the uncertainty set is a TV ball with inequality radius
nonclaims: the lower envelope across several codes need not itself be concave
unused TV radius after saturation is not treated as an error in the certificate

claims.title: Huber contamination inclusion and exact extremal expectation
claims.scope: one finite nominal probability law, one fixed value vector, and a Huber contamination fraction in the unit interval
assumptions: the contaminated law is (1-epsilon) times the nominal law plus epsilon times an arbitrary replacement law
the replacement law may concentrate on an extreme-value state
nonclaims: Huber contamination and a TV ball with the same numerical radius are not identical uncertainty sets
the result does not assign a contamination fraction to empirical data without a sampling model

claims.title: Exact bounded deterministic TV-robust zero-error prefix code
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph, one exact rational nominal prior, one rational TV radius, and all deterministic complete binary zero-error prefix codes below explicit caps
assumptions: every proper independent-set partition and every complete binary prefix shape is exhausted
codebooks inducing the same state-length vector are equivalent for every source prior
the continuous worst-prior inner problem is solved exactly by the mass-transport theorem
nonclaims: the bounded exponential search is not a large-instance runtime guarantee
the deterministic code does not include shared codebook randomness unless that resource is added separately

claims.title: TV-robust coding monotonicity and exact endpoint laws
claims.scope: the deterministic finite TV-robust prefix-code value as the radius ranges from zero to one
assumptions: larger TV balls contain smaller TV balls
at radius zero the ambiguity set contains only the nominal law
at radius one the ambiguity set is the entire finite probability simplex
a maximum-depth d binary prefix tree has at most two to the d leaves
nonclaims: the robust value is not asserted concave in radius because optimal code switches can change slopes
minimum peak prefix length is not the same resource as average traffic or queueing delay

claims.title: Skew K4 exact TV transport and Huber separation
claims.scope: K4 with nominal prior (7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10), state lengths (1,2,3,3), and radius or contamination fraction 1/10
assumptions: the length-one codeword is assigned to the state of nominal probability seven tenths
the full TV ball and Huber contamination set use their declared definitions
nonclaims: the numerical separation is not asserted for every prior and value vector
equal uncertainty parameters do not make Huber and TV sets interchangeable

claims.title: Skew K4 robust-code phase change at TV radius one quarter
claims.scope: K4 with nominal prior (7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10) under deterministic zero-error binary-prefix TV-robust coding
assumptions: all proper partitions and complete prefix shapes are included
ties in robust value are resolved by lower nominal expected length before later canonical criteria
nonclaims: one quarter is specific to the declared prior and code alternatives
the phase change concerns expected prefix length rather than a physical phase transition

claims.title: Bounded exact TV-robust transport and coding audit
claims.scope: bounded rational finite-state TV transport and deterministic robust coding instances checked by the repository
assumptions: seeded denominator-ten simplex grids exhaust every compared adversarial distribution
all sixty-four labeled four-vertex graphs are independently checked over every coloring, complete tree, and feasible grid law
all configured partition, prefix-shape, candidate, and dual checks complete without truncation
nonclaims: bounded exact agreement is not a scalability theorem
a search cap failure is not an optimum, impossibility, or empirical confidence certificate
